analysis.investment_thesis: Neogen Chemicals fails both Magic Formula screens decisively: Earnings Yield of ~2.7% (EBIT ₹136 Cr / EV ~₹5,115 Cr) is a fraction of the 12% minimum, and ROCE of 8.82% is well below the 20%+ threshold for a quality business. The company is in a voracious capex cycle that destroys FCF and inflates the capital base without commensurate earnings growth.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR 25.6% over 9 years — genuine top-line compounding in specialty chemicals
Structural tailwinds: lithium compounds for EV batteries + pharma/agrochem intermediates are secular growth markets
High gross margin (45.85%) indicates genuine pricing power in niche bromination/lithiation chemistry
key_risks: Earnings Yield ~2.7% — stock is priced at 150x P/E and 39x EV/EBITDA, leaving near-zero margin of safety
Borrowings exploded from ₹409 Cr to ₹1,132 Cr in a single year (FY2024→FY2025); finance costs tripled from ₹14 Cr to ₹48 Cr in 4 years, eating net profit
FCF negative in 5 of 6 years (cumulative FCF -₹766 Cr); Capex of ₹318 Cr in FY2025 vs Net Profit of ₹35 Cr — earnings are optical, not cash
red_flags: Net profit declining (₹50 Cr in FY2023 → ₹35 Cr in FY2025) even as revenue grew 13% — interest burden absorbing operating leverage
CWIP jumped to ₹335 Cr in FY2025, signaling another capex wave ahead with no near-term earnings benefit
Other Income swung to -₹10 Cr in FY2025 (from +₹8 Cr prior year) — quality of earnings concern
Debt/Equity of 1.41 with rapidly rising leverage profile makes the balance sheet fragile if capex projects disappoint
analysis.detailed_analysis:
**Magic Formula Verdict — Fails Both Screens:** Earnings Yield = EBIT(₹136 Cr) / EV(~₹5,115 Cr) = 2.7%, versus my 12% minimum. Return on Capital proxied by ROCE = 8.82%, versus my 20% minimum. A company must rank in the top decile on BOTH metrics to earn a buy; Neogen ranks near the bottom on both simultaneously. The P/E of 150x and EV/EBITDA of 39x reflect a market pricing in years of future growth that has not yet materialized in earnings. This is exactly the type of "story stock" the Magic Formula is designed to screen out.

**Capital Cycle Trap:** Neogen's revenue growth is real and impressive, but the business currently resembles a capital-incinerating construction project more than a cash-generative specialty chemicals franchise. Capex of ₹318 Cr in FY2025 against net profit of ₹35 Cr is a 9:1 ratio — the company is reinvesting nine rupees for every rupee it earns. Finance costs have ballooned from ₹14 Cr (FY2021) to ₹48 Cr (FY2025), and borrowings surged ₹723 Cr in a single year. When/if the lithium and bromine capacity comes online and utilization ramps, ROCE could improve materially — but buying at 150x earnings to wait for that rerating is speculation, not Magic Formula investing.
